title: Weekday Surge Anticipation Logbook and Variant Queue
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, operational log and checklist for the small/medium weekday rollout window (non-quiet hours) where we expect transient traffic surges and variant gating. Use as the single source-of-truth for the day-of launch crew. Not a formal runbook — more of a working ledger for the launch operator and telemetry lead.

Release snapshot:
- Release id: v1.12.3
- Target surface: hosted-api (primary), dedicated (patch rollout), private (no change)
- Scope: batching fixes, KV cache improvement, two safety handler bugfixes
- Owners: Priya Nair (release lead), Ethan Park (telemetry), Lena Cho (deploy engineer)
- Rollout window: 2027-07-15 09:00 - 15:00 PDT (weekday window to catch AM peak taper)

High-level intent:
- Gradual canary focused on latency-sensitive routes (/chat, /generate) with variant queueing for model-compatibility fallbacks.
- Observe token tail-latency and top-level 95th percentile across regions; abort or pause if thresholds breached.

Preflight checklist (to complete before 09:00 PDT):
- [ ] Final PR merge and CI green (runtime PR #812).
- [ ] Deployment images built and pinned in registry (sha verified).
- [ ] Canary hosts reserved: 6 GPU instances across us-west-2a/b.
- [ ] Smoke test pack validated in staging (see smoke test tokens below).
- [ ] Alerting subscriptions confirmed for on-call (pager: @infra-oncall).
- [ ] Slack channel created: #release-v1-12-3 (add SRE, infra, telemetry, PM).
- [ ] Linked tickets checked: RD-2345, RD-2420 (no blockers).
- [ ] Rollback artifacts verified and rollback playbook accessible.

Canary ramp & variant queue plan (primary):
- 09:00 PDT: Launch canary at 0.5% global traffic, pinned to model-variant: runtime-v1.12.3-canary. Watch for 10 minutes.
  - Metrics: p95 latency (token step), error rate (5xx + model-fallback), average tokens/sec per host.
  - Abort condition: p95 > baseline + 40% sustained for 5m OR error rate > 0.5% for 10m.
- 09:15 PDT: If green, scale canary to 2% for 15 minutes. Enable prefix KV caching for canary pool.
- 09:35 PDT: Increase to 8% for 20 minutes. Run long-form prompt sample set (10 prompts, 1k tokens each) to stress token cache.
- 10:00 PDT: 25% if steady; run full smoke regression against /chat and /embeddings.
- 10:30 PDT: 60% if stable; prepare for 100% at noon local if no signals.
- 12:00 PDT: Full ramp to 100% (final step) only after 60% for 90 minutes with no threshold hits.

Variant queueing notes:
- If a request cannot be served by the primary model variant due to quantization mismatch, route to fallback 'runtime-v1.11.x-compat' variant.
- Queue depth should remain < 50 per queue per host. If queue depth > 50 and tail-latency climbs, pause traffic ramp and investigate KV eviction rates.

Smoke test pack (staging & canary):
- Basic service checks: /health, /metrics, /models (should list runtime-v1.12.3-canary).
- Functional: 6 short prompts (<64 tokens) across /generate and /chat.
- Stress: 4 long prompts (~1024 tokens) to ensure KV caching behaves.
- Edge: malformed JSON function-calls to ensure graceful failure path maintained.

Rollback matrix (fast paths):
- Fast rollback (immediate): revert to previous sha on deployment group if canary abort condition met. Target recovery time: <8 minutes.
- Throttle rollback: pause increment and reduce canary to previous stable pool for 30 minutes while we triage.
- Emergency evacuation: divert traffic to dedicated gpu pool with older runtime if regional hardware shows issues.

Telemetry and decision criteria (Ethan Park):
- Baselines to compare against: last stable deployment (v1.12.2) p50/p95 token step latency and 5xx rates.
- Telemetry dashboard: per-route latency (p50/p95/p99), model fallbacks, queue depth, host CPU/GPU util.
- SLO thresholds for abort: p95 > baseline*1.4 OR sustained 5xx > 0.5% for 10m OR model-fallbacks > 0.2% for 15m.
- Notify timeline: first suspicious blip -> @telemetry (Ethan), second sustained window -> page SRE.

Communications plan:
- Preflight note (09:00) in #release-v1-12-3 with preflight checklist snapshot.
- Canary pass message at each ramp step in channel.
- On abort: immediate incident thread with title 'v1.12.3 canary abort — <metric> breached' and include rollback action.
- Post-release 1h and 6h summaries posted to Confluence and linked in the channel.

Infra & capacity notes (Lena Cho):
- Autoscaler policy slightly relaxed for the canary pool to avoid rapid thrash; set min_replicas=2, max_replicas=8 for canary.
- KV cache debug logging enabled at INFO for canary only; retain for 3h, then auto toggle off.
- Disk and GPU health check before scale up (script at infra/health/check_gpu.sh).

Release notes draft (to publish after successful rollout):
- Title: v1.12.3 — latency-focused improvements and stability fixes
- Highlights:
  - Reduced token tail latency for common chat prompts via smarter KV prefetching.
  - Fix: runtime crash when handling nested function-calls with empty args.
  - Fix: rare cascade where batching window extended causing token duplication under high throughput.
- Backwards compatibility: No client-facing API changes. Model variant fallback maintained.
- Known issues: Small subset of very long (>8k token) prompts may see marginally higher memory usage — tracking RD-2420.

Day-of operational log (fillable):
- 2027-07-15 08:50 Priya: final CI green, images pushed sha: abc123def
- 2027-07-15 09:02 Lena: canary pool started (6 hosts)
- 2027-07-15 09:12 Ethan: observed p95 +15% (within tolerance).
- 2027-07-15 09:18 Priya: ramp to 2%
- 2027-07-15 09:40 Ethan: KV eviction spike at 09:36 — investigating (note: TTL misestimate in test harness)
- 2027-07-15 09:55 Lena: increased canary to 8% after TTL tweak
- [space for further entries]

Open questions & action items (pre/post):
- [ ] Confirm long-prompt memory regression fix timeline (owner: Samira Hussein).
- [ ] Decide whether to enable extended KV debug logging for dedicated pools after roll.
- [ ] Product: confirm no rollout-specific messaging needed for high-throughput customers (PM: @james).

Post-release monitoring & checkpoints:
- 0–1h: close watch on p95, 5xx, and model-fallbacks (telemetry cadence: 5m).
- 1–6h: medium watch, cadence 15m, run synthetic long-prompt job every hour.
- 24h: stability sign-off meeting if no regressions.
- If any regression observed after rollout: open postmortem linked to RD-PT-<date>.

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep the canary conservative for weekday surges; peak-to-trough is noisy.
- If queue depth climbs but 5xx doesn't, consider reducing batch window rather than immediate rollback.
- Keep communication short and prescriptive in the channel — operators need clear next actions.

Appendix: quick commands & references
- Deploy command (internal): ./scripts/deploy-canary --image=registry.redwood/v1.12.3-canary --pool=release-canary-2027-07
- Rollback: ./scripts/roll-deploy --group=release-canary-2027-07 --to-sha=previous
- Health scripts: infra/health/check_gpu.sh, infra/telemetry/emit_smoke_set.sh

End of working ledger. Add entries during day-of and consolidate into release notes post-6h summary.
